subject: SIG: Warm-standby recovery — RTO/RPO, backups, and cross-region failover (follow-up)
messages:
From: Hannah Levy <hannah.levy@healthsync.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: SIG: Warm-standby RTO/RPO clarifications

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the SIG submission. Our security team is reviewing the BCDR section and has a few follow-ups before we sign off. Can you confirm the following specific items for our records: 

- Measured RTO for the public inference API (99th pct) when failing over to a warm-standby region.
- Measured RPO for: (a) user KV/state (small TTL caches), (b) persistent user artifacts (file uploads), and (c) model artifacts/weights.
- Backup cadence and retention for primary DBs and object storage, plus last successful restore test (date/timestamp and summary).
- Cross-region failover steps (DNS, automation, manual steps) and expected time-to-traffic shift.
- Whether encryption keys (KMS/HSM) are replicated or require manual rekey during failover.

If you can provide a short summary and attach any evidence (playbook excerpts, test logs, diagrams) that would be ideal. We are on a timeline to complete SIG in two weeks.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30m call if easier.

Best,
Hannah
Security Lead, HealthSync

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Levy <hannah.levy@healthsync.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T11:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Warm-standby RTO/RPO clarifications

Hi Hannah —

Thanks — below is a concise summary addressing each bullet. I also attached a short "BCDR summary" PDF and a link to our warm-standby playbook (playbook-warm-standby.md). If you want a deeper evidence package we can include the full DR test export.

Summary answers (high-level):
- Public inference API (99th pct during failover): measured RTO = ~15 minutes to route traffic and have pre-warmed workers accept requests via warm-standby automation. This assumes advertised DNS TTLs and Route53 health-checks are in place.
- RPO:
  * user KV/state (ephemeral caches/redis-style): typical RPO <= 5 minutes; we persist critical KV to durable store with async replication.
  * persistent user artifacts (S3 object store): RPO <= 15 minutes under our cross-region replication; objects are uploaded to a primary bucket with cross-region replication (CRR) to the warm region.
  * model artifacts/weights: RPO effectively ~0 — model artifacts are synchronously replicated to our artifact store (object storage + checksum verification) and pre-staged in the warm region during normal operations (artifact push pipeline runs on each model release).
- Backups & retention: daily full snapshots for DBs, hourly incremental snapshots for the last 7 days, and point-in-time logs retained for 14 days; object storage snapshots/versions retained for 90 days. Full retention policy attached in the PDF.
- Last successful restore test: 2026-09-14T14:08:33-07:00 — we exercised a warm-standby failover and completed validation tests (see attached dr-runbook-20260914-incident.log and the DR test summary link).
- Cross-region failover steps (high-level): automated failover triggers health-check alert -> Route53 failover routing policy flips to warm region -> autoscaling group in warm region promotes read replicas and warm workers load models from pre-staged artifacts -> post-failover verification runs (synthetic requests and checksum validation). Time-to-traffic shift observed in last test: ~12–18 minutes depending on DNS propagation and client-side caching.
- KMS/keys: Customer data keys are stored in a KMS-backed envelope; we replicate key metadata but not HSM hardware. In practice, we have: replicated KMS keys (CloudKMS/custom KMS replication) with predefined IAM roles in the warm region so no manual rekey is required for failover. We included a kms-replication-diagram.pdf for the key flow.

Attachments included: bcdr-summary-2026Q3.pdf, playbook-warm-standby.md, kms-replication-diagram.pdf

If you want explicit measured timelines from the 2026-09-14 run I can pull the test export and attach the logs.

Best,
Priyom
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Levy <hannah.levy@healthsync.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T08:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Warm-standby RTO/RPO clarifications

Thanks Priyom — that summary is helpful. Two follow-ups: 

1) For "persistent user artifacts" (S3 CRR) can you confirm whether object metadata (ACLs, encryption headers) are preserved in replication and how data consistency is verified after failover?
2) For KMS replication — are customer-managed keys (CMKs) replicated, or only service-managed keys? We need to note this distinction for our compliance team.

If possible, can you also provide the raw DR test timeline (timestamps for trigger, cutover, verification complete) from the 2026-09-14 run? That will speed our review.

We may request a brief joint call with your ops lead to walk through the runbook.

—Hannah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Levy <hannah.levy@healthsync.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-06T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Warm-standby RTO/RPO clarifications

Hi Hannah —

Quick notes to confirm:
- S3 CRR: ACLs and server-side encryption headers are replicated as part of CRR; object metadata is preserved. After failover we run an object-level checksum verification against a sampling of critical buckets (scripted as part of the playbook).
- KMS: service-managed CMKs used for platform telemetry are replicated; customer-managed keys require customer configuration for cross-region replication (we document the required IAM trust relationship and provide a Scripted guide). If you use CMKs we can include the explicit instructions in the evidence package.

I will attach the DR test run log (dr-runbook-20260914-incident.log) and the test timeline CSV in the next message. Vivek is looping in infra to provide the timeline export.

—Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Highlights from the 2026-09-14 run (copied from the log):

- 14:10:02 Route53 automated failover engaged
- 14:18:45 Warm workers in secondary reached steady-state and started accepting traffic
- 14:22:01 Post-failover validation completed (synthetic checks, checksum sampling)

Best,
Priyom
